title: If Tyler Biadasz is out long term for the Chargers, Jarrett Patterson (HOU) and Daniel Brunskill (WAS) are two options that could be cut in a couple weeks that make sense to come in and back up Jake Slaughter. Brunskill has spent multiple seasons with McDaniel (4 in SF and 1 in MIA) so there would not be any schematic learning curve, and he can play all 3 interior spots. Patterson has some scheme familiarity from his time with Slowik (and Shane Day) from 2023 and 2024. He could play all 3 spots on the interior as well. He also played two seasons at Notre Dame with Joe Alt. Either way, would prefer to get a veteran backup in here even though Jacob Spomer did some nice things on tape last week.

Dobbins, RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman -- since Sean Payton has talked about the difficulty of making it work with a 3-RB rotation. "I think it's all gonna work itself out, but yes, I've had a lot of those thoughts, especially watching Jonah play the way he has the last few weeks, and we all know what J.K. is, and RJ had 12 touchdowns as a rookie," Webb said. "I think there's worse issues out there. We'll try to figure it out, and I know Sean will be a great voice to lean on when those conversations come up in game-plan meetings."

title: EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 14, a joint joint with the LA Chargers: - In the long history of joint practices, this might have been the most peaceful. I didn't see a single fight and, at least on the 49ers O vs. Chargers D end, nothing that even came close. It did lead to the best line of the day, from Kyle Shanahan who was asked why things seemed to be calmer today. With tongue firmly in cheek, Shanahan said "No, their head coach has more discipline than Tennessee's." Shanahan was, of course, poking fun at his friend Robert Saleh after the Niners and Titans had a number of skirmishes last week. - The caveat here is that I was only able to watch 49ers O vs. Chargers D. My guy @krisrhim1 was on the other end keeping an eye on the 49ers D against the Chargers O. - DT C.J. West and DL Titus Leo both suffered concussions in practice on Sunday. West did not practice today. Leo was waived/injured to make room on the roster for the re-signing of DT Evan Anderson. - DL Keion White (adductor), RB Kaelon Black (adductor) and WR Demarcus Robinson (undisclosed) were back at practice today. White did not do everything while Black was very involved. Robinson only missed the one practice on Sunday. - One other new addition to list of non participants: WR Malik Turner. Did not see him when taking attendance. - Here's the list of non participants on Tuesday: West, Turner, G Dominick Puni (concussion), DT Gracen Halton (ankle), RB Christian McCaffrey (tightness), LB Luke Gifford (hamstring), DE Nick Bosa (soreness/tendinitis), FB Kyle Juszczyk (broken finger), OL Brett Toth (concussion), QB Kurtis Rourke (undisclosed/ribs), WR Christian Kirk (calf), S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), RB Jordan James (rib), OT Vederian Lowe (ankle), CB Nate Hobbs (groin) Players on PUP: TE George Kittle (achilles), RB Isaac Guerendo (pec), DL Mykel Williams (ACL) - WR Mike Evans took part in a big chunk of practice before he walked to the side, got his left foot and ankle taped and iced up and took of his jersey and shoulder pads. He then walked back on to the field, seemingly in good spirits, and walked to the sideline. There, he removed the ice pack and moved it to his left quad. Shanahan said Evans had some tightness and the team wanted to be smart with him. He didn't sound concerned nor did it look particularly painful for Evans, but we'll see where he is when the team returns to practice this weekend. Hard to imagine he will play (or would have) on Thursday night. - Speaking of, Shanahan said the plan is for some of the starters to play and indicated that QB Brock Purdy would likely be one of those who do. Doubt it will be for long but could get a look at Purdy on Thursday night. - That could be a good thing for the Niners offense because, by my estimation, the Chargers defense won the day. The 49ers started off pretty well with Purdy completing 8 of his first 11 passes with a mix of intermediate strikes and short connections and with Black showing his fresh legs. Black had one burst off the left side that might have gone for a long touchdown run in a real game. Purdy hit Evans multiple times for chunks and also found Robinson for a couple of sizable gains. - From there, however, the Chargers seemed to flex their defensive muscle, aided by a strong showing from their front. Leading the charge (pun unmercifully intended) was Tuli Tuipulotu. He was outstanding setting an edge in the run game but also was getting off blocks to make the stops as well. I had him down for multiple run stuffs as well as at least part of a would-be sack. My unsolicited advice to the Chargers: pay that man his money. - Among the other Chargers defensive plays worth noting: a run stuff from LB Troy Dye, who also had a pair of nice PBUs, including one in which he got fingertips on a throw from Purdy for Stribling that would have been a huge gain if not for Dye. DL TerRah Edwards had a run stuff against Black, Khalil Mack had a would-be sack and DL Nick Barrett batted a pass at the line of scrimmage from Mac Jones. CB Isas Waxter made a nice break on a throw from Jones for Jordan Watkins for an interception. Watkins seemed to either stumble out of his break or was just slow doing it as Waxter made the pick. OLB Andre Carter blew past Enrique Cruz Jr. for what would have been an easy sack. And perhaps the biggest play of the day came when LB Del'Shawn Phillips intercepted Purdy on a throw over the middle for TE Luke Farrell. S Derwin James got a hand in to deflect it for Phillips to make the pick. Shanahan's assessment of the session for the offense: "I liked it a little more at first, didn't like it as much later," Shanahan said. "I thought we struggled a little bit in the move-the-ball periods, didn't score in two-minute, so there were some ups and downs, but I didn't really like how we finished the day.” - It wasn't perfect for Stribling but he caught a pair of touchdowns, including an impressive grab over Waxter on a jump ball from Jones. He also hauled in a crosser from Purdy for a score. - WR Trenton Irwin made an outstanding catch deep down the sideline in which he toe tapped while being shoved out of bounds and got the catch. He had a few catches today, including a deep one down the middle from Jones. - Carver Willis continues to get a long look in the LG competition. Purdy on Willis: "I think he's done a good job with coming in. There's a lot within our offensive run scheme and everything. As a young guy to come in and learn that quick, it's a challenge. I think he's been able to handle it pretty well and I know he's going to keep getting better with more reps, but any guy that is in front of me, I'm going to have their back and I know they're going to give it their all for me. So I'm going to keep believing in them, working with them. I’ve got a lot of trust in him.” - Black clearly had fresh legs and had some big gains early in addition to the one potential touchdown. He also made a nice catch in traffic from Jones in the red zone that likely would have been a score. He's expected to play on Thursday night, which is great news for him as he has a real shot to assert himself for the RB2 job. - Mike Shanahan was in attendance today and spent some time chatting with Mac Jones during a special teams period. - That'll do it from SoCal. Niners will play the Chargers on Thursday night and then are slated to be back in Santa Clara for practices this weekend. Thanks for reading.
summary:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 14, a joint joint with the LA Chargers:

- In the long history of joint practices, this might have been the most peaceful. I didn't see a single fight and, at least on the 49ers O vs. Chargers D end, nothing that even came close. 

It did lead to the best line of the day, from Kyle Shanahan who was asked why things seemed to be calmer today. With tongue firmly in cheek, Shanahan said "No, their head coach has more discipline than Tennessee's." Shanahan was, of course, poking fun at his friend Robert Saleh after the Niners and Titans had a number of skirmishes last week. 

- The caveat here is that I was only able to watch 49ers O vs. Chargers D. My guy @krisrhim1 was on the other end keeping an eye on the 49ers D against the Chargers O. 

- DT C.J. West and DL Titus Leo both suffered concussions in practice on Sunday. West did not practice today. Leo was waived/injured to make room on the roster for the re-signing of DT Evan Anderson. 

- DL Keion White (adductor), RB Kaelon Black (adductor) and WR Demarcus Robinson (undisclosed) were back at practice today. White did not do everything while Black was very involved. Robinson only missed the one practice on Sunday. 

- One other new addition to list of non participants: WR Malik Turner. Did not see him when taking attendance.

- Here's the list of non participants on Tuesday:  West, Turner, G Dominick Puni (concussion), DT Gracen Halton (ankle),  RB Christian McCaffrey (tightness), LB Luke Gifford (hamstring), DE Nick Bosa (soreness/tendinitis), FB Kyle Juszczyk (broken finger), OL Brett Toth (concussion), QB Kurtis Rourke (undisclosed/ribs), WR Christian Kirk (calf), S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), RB Jordan James (rib), OT Vederian Lowe (ankle), CB Nate Hobbs (groin)  

Players on PUP: TE George Kittle (achilles), RB Isaac Guerendo (pec), DL Mykel Williams (ACL)

- WR Mike Evans took part in a big chunk of practice before he walked to the side, got his left foot and ankle taped and iced up and took of his jersey and shoulder pads. He then walked back on to the field, seemingly in good spirits, and walked to the sideline. There, he removed the ice pack and moved it to his left quad. Shanahan said Evans had some tightness and the team wanted to be smart with him. He didn't sound concerned nor did it look particularly painful for Evans, but we'll see where he is when the team returns to practice this weekend. Hard to imagine he will play (or would have) on Thursday night. 

- Speaking of, Shanahan said the plan is for some of the starters to play and indicated that QB Brock Purdy would likely be one of those who do. Doubt it will be for long but could get a look at Purdy on Thursday night. 

- That could be a good thing for the Niners offense because, by my estimation, the Chargers defense won the day. The 49ers started off pretty well with Purdy completing 8 of his first 11 passes with a mix of intermediate strikes and short connections and with Black showing his fresh legs. Black had one burst off the left side that might have gone for a long touchdown run in a real game. Purdy hit Evans multiple times for chunks and also found Robinson for a couple of sizable gains. 

- From there, however, the Chargers seemed to flex their defensive muscle, aided by a strong showing from their front. Leading the charge (pun unmercifully intended) was Tuli Tuipulotu. He was outstanding setting an edge in the run game but also was getting off blocks to make the stops as well. I had him down for multiple run stuffs as well as at least part of a would-be sack. My unsolicited advice to the Chargers: pay that man his money. 

- Among the other Chargers defensive plays worth noting: a run stuff from LB Troy Dye, who also had a pair of nice PBUs, including one in which he got fingertips on a throw from Purdy for Stribling that would have been a huge gain if not for Dye. DL TerRah Edwards had a run stuff against Black, Khalil Mack had a would-be sack and DL Nick Barrett batted a pass at the line of scrimmage from Mac Jones. CB Isas Waxter made a nice break on a throw from Jones for Jordan Watkins for an interception. Watkins seemed to either stumble out of his break or was just slow doing it as Waxter made the pick. OLB Andre Carter blew past Enrique Cruz Jr. for what would have been an easy sack. And perhaps the biggest play of the day came when LB Del'Shawn Phillips intercepted Purdy on a throw over the middle for TE Luke Farrell. S Derwin James got a hand in to deflect it for Phillips to make the pick. 

Shanahan's assessment of the session for the offense: 

"I liked it a little more at first, didn't like it as much later," Shanahan said. "I thought we struggled a little bit in the move-the-ball periods, didn't score in two-minute, so there were some ups and downs, but I didn't really like how we finished the day.”

- It wasn't perfect for Stribling but he caught a pair of touchdowns, including an impressive grab over Waxter on a jump ball from Jones. He also hauled in a crosser from Purdy for a score. 

- WR Trenton Irwin made an outstanding catch deep down the sideline in which he toe tapped while being shoved out of bounds and got the catch. He had a few catches today, including a deep one down the middle from Jones. 

- Carver Willis continues to get a long look in the LG competition. Purdy on Willis: 

"I think he's done a good job with coming in. There's a lot within our offensive run scheme and everything. As a young guy to come in and learn that quick, it's a challenge. I think he's been able to handle it pretty well and I know he's going to keep getting better with more reps, but any guy that is in front of me, I'm going to have their back and I know they're going to give it their all for me. So I'm going to keep believing in them, working with them. I’ve got a lot of trust in him.”

- Black clearly had fresh legs and had some big gains early in addition to the one potential touchdown. He also made a nice catch in traffic from Jones in the red zone that likely would have been a score. He's expected to play on Thursday night, which is great news for him as he has a real shot to assert himself for the RB2 job. 

- Mike Shanahan was in attendance today and spent some time chatting with Mac Jones during a special teams period. 

- That'll do it from SoCal. Niners will play the Chargers on Thursday night and then are slated to be back in Santa Clara for practices this weekend. Thanks for reading.

title: Day 16 -- Joint practice vs. 49ers Overall: I watched the offense today. It was perhaps the best the unit has looked this offseason, with Justin Herbert picking apart the 49ers secondary and generating explosive plays throughout practice. The offensive line was strong in the run game but inconsistent in pass protection. The caveat of the big passing day is that several of the offense’s biggest plays may have been nullified or looked different in a game, when defenders are allowed to hit the quarterback because the niners d line got pressure throughout. Most notably Osa Odighizuwa, who I charted with four pressures the most of any defender Notes - The offensive line had a strong day run blocking, consistently creating lanes for the running backs. Omarion Hampton took advantage, running over 49ers defenders S Ji'Ayir Brown and LB Jaden Duggar on two carries - Quentin Johnston had the catch of the day, making a one-handed grab while CB Deommodore Lenoir grabbed him and was flagged for pass interference. This was the play on which Tyler Biadasz suffered his injury. - Left guard Kayode Awosika blocked Sebastion Valdez Biadasz's left left leg. Trainers worked on Biadasz for around five minutes before helping him onto a medical cart where he exited practice. Jake Slaughter moved to center with him out. - Johnston later appeared to tweak his right ankle/lower leg while attempting a leaping catch. He remained at practice but did not return to team periods. - Brenen Thompson had a big day with two 50-plus-yard touchdowns. The first came from Herbert, though Osa Odighizuwa got to Herbert before the pass was released and the play likely would've been different in a game. Odighizuwa tapped Herbert after blowing by Trey Pipkins well before Herbert released the ball. Thompson's second came on a deep ball from DJ Uiagalelei, though DL Romello Height beat OL Logan Taylor. - Odighizuwa was a problem throughout practice. I had him down for four pressures, the most of any 49ers defender. - David Njoku scored on what appeared to be a coverage bust, with no defender near him. - Ladd McConkey had a similar reception on an apparent coverage bust, though Odighizuwa beat Branson Taylor for pressure on the play. McConkey was consistently open throughout practice and caught multiple touchdowns, including one through a hold by Jack Jones during a red-zone period. - Herbert's best red-zone throw may have been to McConkey. Rolling left, Herbert threw back across his body and found McConkey between two defenders for a touchdown. - Jack Jones nearly intercepted Trey Lance during a separate 11-on-11 period but dropped the pass. - JaQuae Jackson caught a deep ball from Lance, though James Thompson Jr. generated pressure after beating Slaughter at center. - Fred Warner punched the ball out of Njoku's hands after a catch, forcing a fumble. - Kayode Awosika, Slaughter and Branson Taylor all took reps at left guard. After Biadasz's injury, Slaughter moved exclusively to center. Slaughter's play at center fluctuated. I had him down for holds on back-to-back plays during the final 11-on-11 period after he was beaten by Odighizuwa and Sam Okuayinonu. - Kyle Kennard limped out of practice with a trainer. - 49ers DT Sebastian Valdez easily beat Jake Slaughter for what would have been a TFL during an 11-on-11 period. - WR Dalevon Campbell caught a couple of touchdowns during the red-zone period. - In addition to Odighizuwa, Thompson Jr. and Ogbo Okoronkwo generated multiple pressures - Akheem Mesidor has now missed three straight practicies. Rashawn Slater has missed eight. Tarheeb Still hasn't participated in team int he last eight. Third day of missed practice for Tre' Harris, second for Donte Jackson.

title: 49ers - Chargers in the books. What a treat that practice was. Harbaugh, Shanahan, Purdy, Herbert and so much more... Highlights and *context*: 🏈49ers defense obviously needs Nick Bosa, but thankfully do they have Osa. SF struggled to set edges early; that led to some big Keaton Mitchell runs and play-action success for Herbert and Co. — including wide-open David Njoku TD and a Quentin Johnson TD vs Deommodore Lenoir 🏈That said, some of the deep-ball highlight clips (like Herbert to Brenen Thompson over Ji'Ayir Brown) floating online would've been Odighizuwa sacks. He lived in LA's backfield — but couldn't touch Herbert since it was practice 🏈Kaelon Black is back and has **impressive** burst. Immediately noticed the difference between him and 49ers' backup RBs of recent practices. Black also looks stronger than 208 pounds — that's a lot of muscle moving at a high rate of speed 🏈In red zone, 49ers QB Adrian Martinez hit Black on an angle route for a TD 🏈De'Zhaun Stribling made a sweet TD grab on a jump-ball fade from Mac Jones in RZ, although the 49ers saw relatively limited success there. They still have all the makings of a very good RZ team. "Hell yeah, Stribbles!" yelled a 49ers' O-linemen 🏈Jones threw an INT to LA CB Eric Rogers earlier. Pass was intended for 49ers WR Jordan Watkins, who was outmuscled by the 6-2 Rogers. Watkins later couldn't hold onto a desperation RZ heave from Purdy in the end zone that certainly gave him a chance 🏈In general, Jones has not been overly accurate this camp, but there were also misfires last year at this time. The guy proved himself as a gamer last season and the 49ers aren't worried 🏈Treated to a few Trent Williams vs Khalil Mack reps. Walking Hall of Famers 🏈Sweet run stuff from 49ers LB Garret Wallow, whom Fred Warner praised heavily, against LA RB Jarret Patterson 🏈49ers offense started hot but finished worse once practice graduated to move-the-ball sessions. Opposite was generally true on the other side, where the 49ers defense started better asserting itself later — included a Fred Warner punch out of Njoku 🏈Chargers DE Andre Carter II, who worked out for the 49ers a couple weeks ago, ripped past SF rookie LT Enrique Cruz Jr. on a RZ rep. Williams helped coached Cruz up a few minutes later 🏈Rookie 49ers DT James Thompson Jr. had an awesome swim move vs LA LG Jake Slaughter. The 6-6 Thompson's stock seems to rise on a daily basis. Fellow rookie DT Bryson Eason, a much wider/stouter frame, also held his ground well vs the run 🏈Early on was a trial-by-fire day for 49ers rookie CB Ephesians Prysock, who was beaten a couple times downfield by Brenen Thompson 🏈No music at practice today so hilarious to listen to Mike Evans lobbying the officials like a truly seasoned HOF-bound vet. Evans left practice early with a wrap around his quad but Shanahan said it was just precautionary 🏈Mike Shanahan in attendance for this practice 🏈Did Jim Harbaugh ever get to meet Brock Purdy? Let's end on that cliffhanger...
summary:
49ers - Chargers in the books. What a treat that practice was. Harbaugh, Shanahan, Purdy, Herbert and so much more... Highlights and *context*:

🏈49ers defense obviously needs Nick Bosa, but thankfully do they have Osa. SF struggled to set edges early; that led to some big Keaton Mitchell runs and play-action success for Herbert and Co. — including wide-open David Njoku TD and a Quentin Johnson TD vs Deommodore Lenoir
🏈That said, some of the deep-ball highlight clips (like Herbert to Brenen Thompson over Ji'Ayir Brown) floating online would've been Odighizuwa sacks. He lived in LA's backfield — but couldn't touch Herbert since it was practice
🏈Kaelon Black is back and has **impressive** burst. Immediately noticed the difference between him and 49ers' backup RBs of recent practices. Black also looks stronger than 208 pounds — that's a lot of muscle moving at a high rate of speed
🏈In red zone, 49ers QB Adrian Martinez hit Black on an angle route for a TD
🏈De'Zhaun Stribling made a sweet TD grab on a jump-ball fade from Mac Jones in RZ, although the 49ers saw relatively limited success there. They still have all the makings of a very good RZ team.
"Hell yeah, Stribbles!" yelled a 49ers' O-linemen
🏈Jones threw an INT to LA CB Eric Rogers earlier. Pass was intended for 49ers WR Jordan Watkins, who was outmuscled by the 6-2 Rogers. Watkins later couldn't hold onto a desperation RZ heave from Purdy in the end zone that certainly gave him a chance
🏈In general, Jones has not been overly accurate this camp, but there were also misfires last year at this time. The guy proved himself as a gamer last season and the 49ers aren't worried
🏈Treated to a few Trent Williams vs Khalil Mack reps. Walking Hall of Famers
🏈Sweet run stuff from 49ers LB Garret Wallow, whom Fred Warner praised heavily, against LA RB Jarret Patterson 
🏈49ers offense started hot but finished worse once practice graduated to move-the-ball sessions. Opposite was generally true on the other side, where the 49ers defense started better asserting itself later — included a Fred Warner punch out of Njoku
🏈Chargers DE Andre Carter II, who worked out for the 49ers a couple weeks ago, ripped past SF rookie LT Enrique Cruz Jr. on a RZ rep. Williams helped coached Cruz up a few minutes later
🏈Rookie 49ers DT James Thompson Jr. had an awesome swim move vs LA LG Jake Slaughter. The 6-6 Thompson's stock seems to rise on a daily basis. Fellow rookie DT Bryson Eason, a much wider/stouter frame, also held his ground well vs the run
🏈Early on was a trial-by-fire day for 49ers rookie CB Ephesians Prysock, who was beaten a couple times downfield by Brenen Thompson
🏈No music at practice today so hilarious to listen to Mike Evans lobbying the officials like a truly seasoned HOF-bound vet. Evans left practice early with a wrap around his quad but Shanahan said it was just precautionary
🏈Mike Shanahan in attendance for this practice 
🏈Did Jim Harbaugh ever get to meet Brock Purdy?

Let's end on that cliffhanger...

title: Mike LaFleur had a lot of interesting things to say about preseason playing time and joint practices today, namely that he's going to try to do multiple joint practices during future camps. If he had could, LaFleur said he'd have three joint practices during training camp. He said coaches were presented with data at the owners meetings in March that showed joint practices are essentially the equivalent of a preseason game because of the "amped-up environment." There's also data, LaFleur said, that shows there's a lower injury risk heading into first four weeks of the season if a team participates in joint practices. However, LaFleur learned two lessons about joint practices early in his head coaching tenure. He started getting calls from other head coaches about holding joint practices on the day he was hired which led him to learn that many teams already had their joint practices scheduled by then. And LaFleur learned that teams don't want to come to Arizona for a joint practice because of the heat and the Cardinals can't host them in State Farm Stadium because of limited space. "If you're not doing any joint practices, which basically no one does anymore, then they need to play a certain amount if you want to follow this model," LaFleur said. "So, again, everyone's going to take their own, deal with it and go from there."

title: Biggest takeaways from Broncos training camp practice today: -Most spirited practice of camp —First real fight of camp, Bo Nix pulled Nik Bonitto off pile by his leg, then Bonitto help back by teammates. Calvin Throckmoeton left practice after head bleeding —Bo Nix got pushed down on a sack, got up and threw the ball in anger —Defense went crazy multiple times for would be huge hits —Offense went crazy for TDs —Second scuffle of Broncos camp during 9on7 -Defense won final situational period of practice in clean sweep -Alex Singleton picked off Bo, then ball punched out for fumble -Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims practiced in full pads -Waddle participated in team -Bo Nix hit Waddle on 30-yard completion perfectly led him -Frank Crum with a catch from Jarrett Stidham -Luke Wattenberg did walkthrough and drills then side field -Drew Sanders, Alex Forsyth & Michael Bandy DNP -Mims went to side field midway
summary:
Biggest takeaways from Broncos training camp practice today:

-Most spirited practice of camp
—First real fight of camp, Bo Nix pulled Nik Bonitto off pile by his leg, then Bonitto help back by teammates. Calvin Throckmoeton left practice after head bleeding
—Bo Nix got pushed down on a sack, got up and threw the ball in anger
—Defense went crazy multiple times for would be huge hits
—Offense went crazy for TDs
—Second scuffle of Broncos camp during 9on7

-Defense won final situational period of practice in clean sweep

-Alex Singleton picked off Bo, then ball punched out for fumble

-Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims practiced in full pads

-Waddle participated in team

-Bo Nix hit Waddle on 30-yard completion perfectly led him

-Frank Crum with a catch from Jarrett Stidham

-Luke Wattenberg did walkthrough and drills then side field

-Drew Sanders, Alex Forsyth & Michael Bandy DNP

-Mims went to side field midway
